newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO's Solana leaves on visit to U.S.
newsitem.headline: NATO's Solana leaves on visit to U.S.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana left Brussels on Wednesday for a two-day visit to the United States for talks on the alliance's plans to expand eastwards and its future relations with Russia.
Solana, the man charged with negotiating a new NATO-Russia accord, is due to meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and senior administration officials.

The talks, which will also focus on plans to change the alliance's command structure to allow it to take on more Bosnia-style peacekeeping missions, take place a few days before Solana goes to Moscow for a new round of negotiations.
Solana is to hold talks on Tuesday next week with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov on a document setting out a new post-Cold War relationship between the former enemies.

The deal is currently stalled over Moscow's demands the Western alliance agree not to build new military facilities on the territory of potential new NATO members such as Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
